firing.source: function f() { if (a) { return 1; } else { return 2; } }

findings.message: This `else` follows a branch that always returns, so it is doing nothing. The code after it only runs when the `if` did not return, which is what an `else` says, and the extra nesting costs the reader a level of indentation to learn nothing.

clean.source: function f() { if (a) { return 1; } else if (b) { return 2; } }
